title: FMVSS barrier review
summary: NHTSA requested public input on whether federal vehicle safety standards written for human-driver controls or seating positions could pose unnecessary barriers to automated-driving vehicles. The notice sought examples of affected provisions and possible revisions but did not propose specific binding regulatory text or change any existing certification requirements.

title: Removing regulatory barriers for ADS vehicles
summary: NHTSA requested detailed input on adapting crash-avoidance safety standards for vehicles equipped with automated driving systems that may lack conventional driver controls. The advance notice explored how to preserve safety performance while rethinking driver-oriented specifications and tests; it did not itself amend any standard or authorize driverless deployment.

title: Occupant protection proposal
summary: NHTSA proposed revising eleven occupant crash-protection standards to accommodate automated-driving vehicles without conventional steering wheels and driver seats. Proposed changes would revise seat terminology, crash-test references, steering-system applicability and protections for occupantless cargo vehicles. NHTSA later finalized a revised package affecting thirteen standards in March 2022.

title: Occupant protection final rule
summary: NHTSA amended thirteen occupant protection standards for vehicles equipped with automated driving systems and lacking traditional human driving controls. The March 2022 final rule updates driver-seat and steering references, test procedures and selected applicability provisions while retaining crash protections for passengers; it does not establish automated-driving performance or operational safety standards.

title: Steering control rearward displacement · FMVSS 204
summary: NHTSA's final rule exempts vehicles certified to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 208's frontal-barrier crash-protection provisions from the steering-column rearward displacement test of Standard 204. This generally applicable vehicle-design amendment removes obsolete requirements; it is separate from the 2022 change for automated vehicles with no steering column.

title: Transmission displays · FMVSS 102
summary: NHTSA proposes to exempt vehicles equipped with automated driving systems and no manual driving controls from the requirement to display transmission shift positions to a human driver. The proposal addresses human-facing transmission indicators, not the vehicle's underlying transmission safety or automated driving performance.

title: Defrosting and windshield wiping · FMVSS 103/104
summary: NHTSA proposes to exempt vehicles designed for automated driving without conventional manual driving controls from selected windshield defrosting, defogging, wiping, and washing requirements intended to maintain a human driver's view. The proposal covers Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards 103 and 104; it is not yet an adopted exemption.

title: Tire placards · FMVSS 110
summary: NHTSA proposes changing tire and loading information placard rules for vehicles without a conventional driver's side. Instead of requiring placement specifically on the driver's side, the proposed amendment would permit the placard on the left side of these vehicles. The proposal concerns vehicle labeling, not tire performance requirements.

title: Brake controls · FMVSS 135
summary: NHTSA proposes removing requirements for hand- or foot-operated service-brake controls from vehicles designed to be driven exclusively by automated driving systems. It would also adapt brake warnings, parking-brake controls and test procedures for vehicles without a human driver's position, while retaining the standard's braking-performance protections.

title: FMVSS 201 · Interior impact
summary: The 2022 final rule adapts interior-impact occupant protection tests and seat-position references to vehicles without conventional steering wheels or driver seats. Requirements now use vehicle seating layouts and occupant positions, rather than assuming a human-driven left-front seat. Crashworthiness protections continue to apply wherever a vehicle is designed to carry people.

title: FMVSS 203 · Steering control impact
summary: The rule excludes vehicles designed without steering controls from the steering-control impact standard, because there is no steering wheel or column for occupants to strike. Vehicles equipped with conventional steering controls remain subject to applicable impact requirements; this is a design-specific exemption, not a blanket waiver of occupant crash protection.

title: FMVSS 204 · Steering control rearward displacement
summary: The rule removes application of the steering-column rearward displacement test to vehicles without steering controls, where the test has no relevant component. The 2022 amendment is limited to driverless-control designs; a separate 2026 rule later addressed steering-column displacement requirements for certain vehicles certified under the frontal crash standard.

title: FMVSS 205 · Glazing materials
summary: The final rule clarifies glazing-material requirements for vehicles built without human occupants, including an amended application to trucks designed to carry at least one person. Occupant-protection glazing requirements continue where vehicles carry people; the rule does not create new performance standards for automated driving or sensors.

title: FMVSS 206 · Door locks and retention
summary: The rule revises door-lock and door-retention terminology and applicability for vehicles with no conventional driver's seat or manual steering controls. It uses physical seating and door locations instead of human-driver references, retaining relevant door-retention crash protection for passenger-carrying vehicles, including driverless designs.

title: FMVSS 207 · Seating systems
summary: The final rule changes seating-system requirements and definitions so a vehicle is not assumed to have a designated driver's seat unless manually operated driving controls are present. Seat strength, anchorage and other relevant passenger seating protections remain in force for automated vehicles built to transport people.

title: FMVSS 208 · Occupant crash protection
summary: The rule extensively revises occupant crash-protection terms, airbag suppression requirements, test-dummy placement and front-row seating references for vehicles without human driving controls. It clarifies protection of front-center and other inboard positions and retains occupant protection performance standards; NHTSA did not adopt a proposed child-detection vehicle-motion suppression requirement.

title: FMVSS 212 · Windshield mounting
summary: The final rule amends windshield-mounting standard applicability to exclude trucks not designed to carry any person. Because this standard protects occupants from windshield separation during a crash, NHTSA determined it need not apply to occupantless cargo vehicles. The requirement remains applicable to passenger-carrying vehicle configurations.

title: FMVSS 214 · Side impact protection
summary: The rule replaces driver-based side-impact test references with front-row, left-side and right-side seating positions where necessary for vehicles without conventional driver controls. It preserves side-impact protection and crash-test requirements for passenger-carrying automated vehicles, adapting how tests are positioned rather than exempting the vehicle from protection.

title: FMVSS 216a · Roof crush resistance
summary: The rule revises roof-crush resistance terminology, applicability and seating/test-location references for vehicles without traditional driver seats or steering controls. Passenger-carrying automated vehicles remain subject to relevant roof-strength protections, while requirements designed to protect occupants are not applied indiscriminately to vehicles built to carry no people.

title: FMVSS 219 · Windshield zone intrusion
summary: NHTSA changed the windshield-zone intrusion standard to exclude trucks designed to carry no person. The rule recognizes that its purpose is to prevent injuries to occupants from components intruding into the windshield area during a crash. Passenger-carrying automated vehicles still must meet applicable intrusion requirements.

title: FMVSS 225 · Child restraint anchorages
summary: The final rule revises the shuttle-bus definition for child-restraint anchorage requirements. In a bus without manually operated driving controls, the single rearward row of forward-facing seats is now referenced relative to all front-row passenger seats, rather than a nonexistent driver's seat; existing applicable child-restraint provisions remain.

title: FMVSS 226 · Ejection mitigation
summary: The rule revises ejection-mitigation applicability, roof and seat-reference definitions and certain test procedures for vehicles without conventional driving controls. NHTSA did not finalize changes to the ejection-mitigation readiness indicator, leaving that issue for a separate potential rulemaking; protection continues for vehicles built to carry people.
